ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left is the net of an octahedron made of 8 triangles, with edges labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and x. The outer edge at the far lower right is labeled x; a horizontal outer edge on the lower left is labeled 5. On the right, a diagram of the octahedron after folding is also shown. Name the vertices from left to right according to the net: the top vertex is U, the left connection point is A, the next upper connection point is B, the lower connection point is C, the next lower connection point is D, the next upper connection point is E, the next lower connection point is F, the upper-right connection point is G, the lower-right connection point is H, and the bottom vertex is J. Thus, x is edge HJ, and 5 is edge CD. Reasoning: The problem states that this net folds into an octahedron. First arbitrarily label the three octahedron vertices of the first triangle UAB as +X, +Y, +Z. In an octahedron, when two adjacent triangles share an edge, the third vertex of the new triangle must be the opposite vertex of the previous third vertex. Propagate along adjacent triangles in the net: UAB -> ABC -> BCD -> BDE -> DEF -> EFG -> FGH -> FHJ. After propagation, C and H are the same octahedron vertex, and D and J are the same octahedron vertex. Therefore edge HJ and edge CD coincide/meet after folding; and CD is exactly the edge labeled 5. So the edge corresponding to x that meets it is 5.

method.method_draft: Use vertex-identification propagation on the octahedron net. From the image, label the net vertices in order: top-left apex U, left junction A, next upper junction B, lower junction C, next lower junction D, next upper junction E, next lower junction F, right upper junction G, right lower junction H, and bottom apex J. The labelled edge x is HJ, and edge 5 is CD. Read from the text that the solid is an octahedron. Assign the first triangular face UAB three octahedron vertex labels, for example +X, +Y, +Z. When crossing a shared edge to an adjacent triangular face in an octahedron, the new third vertex must be the opposite vertex to the previous third vertex across that shared edge. Propagate this along the chain of adjacent triangles in the image: UAB -> ABC -> BCD -> BDE -> DEF -> EFG -> FGH -> FHJ. This gives C and H the same octahedron vertex label, and D and J the same octahedron vertex label. Therefore the boundary edge HJ labelled x is the same final octahedron edge as CD, which is labelled 5.

method.method_draft: Use the dual graph of the octahedron. From the image, treat each small triangle of the net as a face-node and connect two face-nodes when the triangles share an edge. The visible net forms a path of eight faces from the top-left triangle to the bottom-right triangle containing x. Read the text to know these eight faces are the eight faces of an octahedron. The dual graph of an octahedron is a cube, so the path of eight faces in the net is a Hamiltonian path on a cube; the missing cube edges correspond exactly to pairs of cut boundary edges that must meet when folded. Place the eight face-nodes of the net on the cube in the order forced by the alternating shared edges in the strip. Then locate the missing dual adjacency involving the face that has edge x: it pairs that bottom-right face with the earlier face whose exposed boundary edge is labelled 5. Hence the boundary edge meeting x is edge 5.
